newsitem.title: FRANCE: Text of Axa, UAP statement. [CORRECTED 21:41 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Text of Axa, UAP statement. [CORRECTED 21:41 GMT]

text.p: The following is the full text of an English-language statement from French insurers Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) announcing their plans to merge.
"A project aimed at bringing the two groups closer was approved at separate board meetings held earlier today.

"In the face of increasingly stiff glabal competition, the project will enable Axa and UAP to build a group with an unparalleled strategic position that neither insurer could achieve alone. The new group will be the world's second largest insurer and number one worldwide in terms of assets under management.

"Underlying this strategic partnership is a desire to capitalise on the exceptional complementary of business and geographical fit which exists between Axa and UAP. In addition to holding the number one position in France, the group will hold leading positions in the major western European countries. In Great Britain, Belgium, Germany and Spain -- key European insurance markets -- the new group will rank among the leaders. In Italy and the Netherlands, this alliance will make it possible to achieve the requisite critical mass. The new group will also be well-positioned in the US, Canada and Asia/Pacific.

"The partnership will also create significant economies of scale and synergies which will make possible a streamlining of operations in a number of areas, including risk management, asset management, reinsurance and access to the world's capital markets, enhancing overall profitability.
"The new group will feature the industry's most highly-skilled teams, and will have a greater capacity for innovation and additional resources for servicing customers.
"The partnership will take the form of an exchange offer followed by a merger (corrects description of the merger).
UAP shareholders will be offered the opportunity to exchange 10 UAP shares for four Axa shares plus four certificates of guaranteed value:

"-- In June 1999, if the Axa share is trading below 392.50 francs per share (i.e. the equivalent of 157 francs per UAP share), each certificate will entitle its bearer to cash payment of the difference.
"-- Cash payout on the certificate is limited to 80 francs per share, or 32 francs per UAP share.
"-- The certificate will be listed, and will have a theoretical value estimated at 47.60 francs, or 19 francs per UAP share.
"Based on the average trading price of UAP stock over the last three months, the deal offers shareholders an immediate global premium of 39 percent.
"This offer is particularly attractive for shareholders of both groups:

"-- UAP shareholders are being offered a substantial premium immediately, with the chance to recover upon maturity a value which is higher than the subscription value offered under the terms of the privatisation. In addition, they will be given the chance to join a group with outstanding development prospects.
"-- For Axa shareholders, this transaction will not jeopardise the short-term profitability of their investment, and boosts their company's growth potential.
"The offer is also of interest to both Axa and UAP customers, as it gives them access to the products and services of an expanded whole."
